top_strength: Garrison kept full control of a genuinely chaotic, rambling customer (mixed-up numbers, mid-sentence tangents, a mom who half-filled out the form) without ever losing his patience or the thread of the call, and he live-adjusted the box-count estimate the moment she corrected herself instead of just plowing through his script. coaching_note: You're leaving real differentiator points on the table — No Worries Damage Coverage and Meet Your Mover never came up, and the Save Your Ass prep speech was skipped entirely even though this customer had until tomorrow afternoon to consolidate and cut her bill. Build those into your close every time, they're not optional add-ons. Also use the customer's name after you get it — you asked for 'Tiffany' up front and then never said it again in 18 minutes, which is an easy, free point on rapport.
phone_presence_notes: Stayed warm and patient through a scattered, tangent-heavy customer, used steady affirmations ('Perfect', 'Absolutely', 'Gotcha, gotcha'), and earned an unprompted 'you're amazing' plus a review commitment from the customer.
